# Estimators, extra worked cases and G10 notes

Companion to [SKILL.md](../SKILL.md). Source tags in parentheses are the citations used in the main file. Items marked
"reader" are this skill's own derivations or inferences, not statements from a source.

## 1. ADF details
- Hamilton canonical form: `y_t = z_1 dy_{t-1} + ... + z_{p-1} dy_{t-p+1} + a + rho y_{t-1} + e_t`, `rho = phi_1 + ... + phi_p`, `z_j = -(phi_{j+1} + ... + phi_p)`. Unit root iff `rho = 1`. Recover levels coefficients: `phi_p = -z_{p-1}`, `phi_j = z_j - z_{j-1}`, `phi_1 = rho + z_1` (Hamilton, Time Series Analysis, 1994, Ch.17).
- Cases (Hamilton Ch.17): 1 no constant, `rho = 1`; 2 constant with `a = 0` under H0; 3 constant with drift under H0; 4 constant plus trend. For a rate or spread level with no drift, use the constant case; use the trend case only for series with a deterministic trend under the alternative (rare in rates).
- Critical values at 5%, T about 164 (Hamilton): case 2 rho-stat -13.8, t -2.89, F 4.68; case 4 rho-stat -21.0, t -3.44, F 6.42. Large T t-stat: -2.86 (constant), -3.41 (trend).
- Worked: log GNP, case 4, 4 lags: `y_t = 0.329 dy_{t-1} + 0.209 dy_{t-2} - 0.084 dy_{t-3} - 0.075 dy_{t-4} + 35.92 + 0.94969 y_{t-1} + 0.0378 t`; ADF rho = -13.3 > -21.0, t = -2.60 > -3.44, F = 3.74 < 6.42: accept unit root. T-bill 1948-89: `rho_hat = 0.96904`, ADF rho -5.74 (crit -13.8), t -1.66 (crit -2.89), F 1.65 (crit 4.68); real dollar-lira ADF t -2.04 (crit -2.88) (Hamilton 1994).
- Tests can conflict: PPP, Engle-Granger `Z_rho -7.54` vs crit -27.1 and `Z_t -2.02` vs -3.80 (no cointegration), Johansen trace 38.85 vs 29.5 (cointegration). Consumption-income `Z_rho -32.0` vs -21.5 (cointegrated). Report both (Hamilton 1994, Ch.20).
- Long memory: `(1-B)^d x_t = a_t`, `-0.5 < d < 0.5`; ACF `rho_k ~ k^(2d-1)`, `rho_1 = d/(1-d)`, spectral density `~ w^(-2d)` near 0 (Tsay, Analysis of Financial Time Series, 2010, s2.11).

## 2. Break and explosiveness family (Lopez de Prado, Advances in Financial Machine Learning, 2018, Ch.17)
- Chow-type Dickey-Fuller: H0 random walk; H1 explosive after `tau* T`. `dy_t = d y_{t-1} D_t[tau*] + e_t`; `DFC = d_hat/s_d`; unknown date `SDFC = sup_{tau*}` over a trimmed range (Andrews 1993). One break only; bubble assumed to last to the end of sample.
- SADF: `dy_t = a + b y_{t-1} + sum g_l dy_{t-l} + e_t`; `SADF_t = sup_{t0 in [1, t-tau]} ADF_{t0,t}`, right end fixed, start expanding backward, `tau` = minimum window. Use log prices (ADF on raw prices implies vol must fall as the price rises).
- Explosive-growth condition for `dlog y = a + b log y_{t-1}`: `b < 0` converges to `-a/b`; `b = 0` unit root; `b > 0` explosive; half-life `-ln2/ln(1+b)`.
- QADF: q-quantile of `{ADF_{t0,t}}` (SADF is q = 1), dispersion `Q_{q+v} - Q_{q-v}`. CADF: tail mean above quantile q (typical q = 0.95), `C <= SADF`; `(SADF - C)/C` large with small `C` flags outliers.
- Sub/super-martingale tests: `SMT_t = sup |b_hat|/(s_b (t-t0)^phi)` for polynomial, exponential and power trend models; phi = 0.5 for the simple case, phi -> 0 favours long weak trends, phi -> 1 short noisy bubbles; feed several phi as features.
- BDE CUSUM depends on the start point; CSW CUSUM on the reference level (use `sup`). SADF is O(n^2).
- Bai-Perron application (Lehman Brothers, LMR Quarterly 2003-Q3, 2003): regress changes of a 5y swap on the third Eurodollar futures contract, the 2y and the 10y swap; break dates chosen by total SSE with regime-specific coefficients; about 10 years of data.

## 3. Volatility extras
- GARCH(1,1) in return notation: `r_t = h_t e_t`, `h_t^2 = a0 + a1 r_{t-1}^2 + b1 h_{t-1}^2`; long-run `h_bar^2 = a0/(1 - b1)` in the Paleologo form for the unrolled recursion `h_t^2 = h_bar^2 + a1 sum_i b1^(i-1) r_{t-i}^2`; MLE minimises `sum (ln h_t^2 + r_t^2/h_t^2)` (Paleologo, The Elements of Quantitative Investing, 2025). The long-run variance of the standard GARCH(1,1) is `a0/(1 - a1 - b1)`; the book's `a0/(1 - b1)` is the long-run level of the recursion's constant term, so use `w/(1 - a - b)` for the variance (reader reconciliation).
- GARCH weaknesses: too much autocorrelation for a given kurtosis and too much long memory (Paleologo 2025). It captures no return autocorrelation, heavy tails and positive ACF of `|r|` and `r^2`.
- Markov-switching vol (Dunis, Laws, Naim, Applied Quantitative Methods for Trading and Investment, 2003): two states, expected high-vol duration `1/(1 - p00)`; standardised residuals can pass Ljung-Box on squares and still fail Jarque-Bera and KS.
- Stochastic vol: `e_t = exp(h_t/2) z_t`, `h_t = g + phi h_{t-1} + eta_t`; Kalman quasi-likelihood on `ln e_t^2`; random-walk case `g = 0, phi = 1` has one parameter (Palomar, Portfolio Optimization, 2025).
- Return decomposition used when relating vol to carry/roll: `dP/P = f dt - D dr + (1/2) C s^2 dt`; forwards equal expected return + `D E(dy)` - `(1/2) C var(dy)`. Risk premium: `E[dP/P] = r0 dt + lambda D dt`, SR `= lambda/sigma`; r0 1%, D 5, lambda 10bp per duration year gives 1.5% expected return, and with 100bp/yr vol SR is 10% (Tuckman and Serrat, Fixed Income Securities, 2022, Ch.8).
- Fat-tail diagnostics for a market panel: excess kurtosis per market, IQR of monthly returns, average max and min monthly returns, pooled histogram vs fitted normal (Macrosynergy, Interest rate swap returns: empirical lessons, 2025).
- Swap Sharpe convention for daily bp changes: `E[r]/sd(r) x sqrt(251)`, no risk-free term; ratings above 1 good, above 2 very good, above 3 outstanding (Burton, Dektor, Wheeler, Time Series Prediction of US Swap Rates, c.2008).

## 4. Kalman and state-space extras
- Embeddings (Hamilton 1994, Ch.13): AR(p): `xi_t = (y_t - mu, ..., y_{t-p+1} - mu)'`, F the companion matrix, `Q` with `s^2` in (1,1), `H' = [1 0 ... 0]`, `R = 0`. MA(1): `xi_t = (e_t, e_{t-1})'`, `F = [[0,0],[1,0]]`, `H' = [1, theta]`. ARMA(p,q): `r = max(p, q+1)`. Representations are not unique but give identical likelihoods.
- Unobserved component (ex-ante real rate): `xi_{t+1} = phi xi_t + v`, observed ex-post real rate `= mu + xi_t + w`, with `w` the inflation-forecast error.
- Parameter uncertainty by Monte Carlo: draw `theta_j ~ N(theta_hat, I^-1/T)`, j = 1..2000; add the average `P` and the outer product of re-filtered states (Hamilton 1994).
- Linear dynamical system and smoother (Bishop, Pattern Recognition and Machine Learning, 2006): `P_{n-1} = A V_{n-1} A' + Gamma`, `K_n = P_{n-1} C' (C P_{n-1} C' + Sigma)^-1`, `mu_n = A mu_{n-1} + K_n (x_n - C A mu_{n-1})`, `V_n = (I - K_n C) P_{n-1}`; RTS smoother uses future data; EM for parameters.
- Local linear trend (Murphy 2012): `A = [[1,1],[0,1]]`, `C = [1,0]`, `Q = diag(Q_a, Q_b)`; seasonal component `c_t = -sum_{s=1}^{S-1} c_{t-s} + e_c`.
- Term-structure state space (Dunis et al. 2003, Ch.3): zero yields at 9 maturities stacked with 9 constant yield-vol equations (18 measurements), diagonal AR(1) transition, stationary `P0` from `vec(P) = (I - F kron F)^-1 (G kron G) vec(Q)`; constraints `0 < phi < 1`, `sigma > 0`. EUR Bund 1986-98: term premium about 1.5 (5y) and 1.6 (10y); factor 2 leads inflation (Granger F 6.12, p = 0.03).
- Macro dynamic factor model (BofA Global Research, US Rates Viewpoint: Introducing a new UST macro framework, 15 Oct 2024): layer 1 is a DFM on 19 macro variables estimating four factors (broad macro, growth, inflation, employment), loadings constrained for meaning, 14 years, weekly; claims, JOLTS and unemployment enter as -1 x z-score. Layer 2 regresses curve PC1 and PC2 on the four factors plus policy rate, central-bank balance sheet and a global yield term: R^2 about 90%+; residual sd about 35bp front end and 20-25bp back end. Fair values at 11 Oct 2024: 2y 4.15% (sd 35bp, 20bp rich, -0.6 sigma), 5y 4.05% (sd 35bp, 15bp rich), 10y 4.15-4.2% (sd 25bp, 10bp rich), 30y 4.35% (sd 20bp, 5bp cheap). The report's 5y exhibit caption (20bp) conflicts with its text (15bp).
- Global-yield state-space fair value (BofA, US Rates Watch: Monthly rates models, Apr and Aug 2025): 10y UST fair value vs global 10y yields about 4.40-4.45%, about 20bp rich (40bp rich in Apr 2025 per the earlier edition); late in the cycle USTs are expected fair-to-rich to global yields.
- Linear models miss stress non-linearities and fail during non-economic buying; add balance-sheet and global-PC1 terms.
- Hidden Markov recursions (Ross, Introduction to Probability Models, 2010): forward `F_n(j) = p(s_n|j) sum_i F_{n-1}(i) P_ij`; filtered `P(X_n = j|s^n) = F_n(j)/sum F_n`; smoothed uses the backward pass; Viterbi path and per-time mode answer different questions.

## 5. Microstructure identities (clean prices before mean-reversion tests)
- Roll: `dp_t = -c q_{t-1} + c q_t + u_t`, `q = +/-1`; `gamma_0 = 2c^2 + s_u^2`, `gamma_1 = -c^2`; `c = sqrt(-gamma_1)`, spread `= 2c`, `s_u^2 = gamma_0 + 2 gamma_1`. Generalised Roll with trade impact `lambda`: `gamma_1 = -c(c + lambda)`; only `s_w^2 = gamma_0 + 2 gamma_1` is identified (Hasbrouck, Empirical Market Microstructure teaching notes, 2004).
- Bid-ask bounce gives negative lag-1 autocovariance, variance ratios above 1 at short horizons, and can make a random walk look stationary. Observed traded prices are not martingales; only the random-walk variance and a lower bound on pricing-error variance are identified. Roll example: 821 trades, `gamma_1 = -0.0000251`, `c = 0.005`, spread $0.01 vs effective spread $0.0158 and quoted $0.022, so Roll underestimates (Hasbrouck 2004).
- MA(1) with `gamma_0 = 1`, `gamma_1 = -0.2`: invertible `theta = -0.2087` (`s_e^2 = 0.958`) and non-invertible `theta = -4.79` (`s_e^2 = 0.0417`) are observationally equal; take |theta| < 1. Beveridge-Nelson: `s_w^2 = theta(1)^2 s_e^2`.
- Variance attribution and information share: `s_w^2 = a Omega a'`; `IS_i = b_i^2 Var(e_i)/s_w^2` if Omega is diagonal, else Cholesky-ordering bounds; structural VAR with `B0` upper triangular (flow hits price contemporaneously); permanent impact = cumulative IRF truncated at 50 transactions, residual-bootstrap CIs (1000 reps) (Fleming, Mizrach, Nguyen, NY Fed Staff Reports No. 381, 2009).
- Interdealer Treasury ECN, 2010-11 (Fleming et al. 2009): permanent impact per $1mm signed volume (256ths) 2y 0.0055, 5y 0.0276, 10y 0.0658, 30y 0.4476; about $363mm moves the 2y one tick, about $8.9mm the 30y. Ignoring limit orders overstates trade impact by 20-50%. Inside spread 1.03 ticks (2y) to 2.66 ticks (30y); event-time liquidity drops around FOMC and 8:30 releases.
- Do not chain overnight returns into intraday models; treat sessions separately and discard the first change (Hasbrouck 2004).

## 6. More worked numbers
- Tsay 2010: 3y on 1y UST level regression R^2 96.5%, coefficient 0.930, residuals strongly serially correlated; change beta about 0.79 (weekly 1962-2009); 3m/6m bill spread cointegrated with error-correction loading about -0.09 per week. Pair example: hedge ratio 0.718, band +/-0.045 (about 1 sigma), 0.09 log-return per round trip before costs, in-sample only; threshold bands must exceed round-trip costs (`2 Delta > eta`).
- Wooldridge, Introductory Econometrics, 2nd ed.: cointegrating slope of the 6m on the 3m bill 1.038 (DOLS), holding-yield ECM speed -0.84 per quarter.
- Swap-rate AR trading (Burton et al. c.2008, 10y, daily bp changes; train about 1994 to late 2007, test to late 2008): buy-and-hold SR 0.25 (0.27 vol-scaled); rolling OLS p = 3, n = 251: 0.23 scaled, 0 unscaled; Burg AR n = 502, p = 4: 0.9. PCA-residual signal (n = 750, p = 4) SR by tenor 2y 0.4, 3y 1.4, 5y 1.2, 7y 2.2, 10y 0.8; singular values [211, 33.6, 12.4, 7.2, 2.4]; the 7y reversion was attributed by the authors to mortgage-servicer hedging.
- Single-stock mean models, 2020 (Palomar 2025): MA(20) on log prices MSE 0.004032 vs MA(20) on log returns 0.000725; i.i.d. 0.000754, AR(1) 0.000793, MA(1) 0.000805, ARMA(1,1) 0.000914; Kalman log-returns dynamic 0.000632, log-prices static 0.000560, dynamic 0.000557. Charting on prices is much worse; whether mean models beat i.i.d. at low autocorrelation is debatable.
- d'Aspremont, Identifying Small Mean Reverting Portfolios, 2008: 100 days US swaps 1Y-30Y; predictability portfolios `lambda` 0.58, 8.61, 16.48, 38.59, 84.55, 174.82, 184.83, 238.11 (p = 0.00 except the last, 0.51); volatilities 0.21, 0.28, 0.34, 0.14, 0.10, 0.09, 0.07, 0.07. Sparse decomposition `lambda` for k = 1..8 legs: 0, 35, 128, 178, 213, 247, 252, 252; optimal 2-leg weights 4Y -0.714, 5Y 0.700. Out-of-sample: 200-day estimation windows re-estimated every 50 days, 1998-2005; a 1bp bid-ask neutralised the edge.
- Sharpe/Ljung-Box/Breusch-Godfrey formulas and the survey of criteria (Mallows `Cp = MSE + (2/n) s^2 (p+1)`, AIC, BIC, LOOCV `(1/n) sum ((Y_i - m_i)/(1 - H_ii))^2`) are in Shalizi, The Truth about Linear Regression (2025) and Greene, Econometric Analysis (2018).

## 7. G10 notes: parameter instability is the rule
The evidence below is about how stable fitted betas are across windows and regimes, which is what the break tests in SKILL.md are for.
All figures from J.P. Morgan Research, Talk is Cheap: Valuing DM Rates Markets with Central Bank Speak (30 May 2024) unless stated.
| Market | Evidence | Time-series consequence |
|---|---|---|
| USD | 1Yx1Y cheapness vs 5y model: R^2 0.840, residual 186.3bp, z 2.80; curve-shape betas to PC1: 0Yx1Y 32bp per 1 sd, 1Yx1Y 17bp, 2Yx1Y 12bp (bear-flattening). SOFR-IORB: regime-weighted log-linear regression in four regimes (BofA, Apr 2025) | one regime-weighted fit, not one window; debt-limit and balance-sheet regimes shift the mean |
| EUR | 1Yx1Y PC1 beta: about -8 long-run, about +10 last 10y, about +5 last 5y. Barbell response to PC1: 0Yx1Y 8.5bp, 1Yx1Y 5.6bp, 3Yx1Y 3.3bp, 10Y/15Yx1Y 4.8bp. Shadow-rate fit below -15% in 2014 is badly identified (Huggins and Schaller 2024) | a long-run beta can have the opposite sign to the recent one: never use a full-sample beta across the negative-rate era without a break test; use the three-step fix for short-rate fits |
| GBP | 1Yx1Y PC1 beta rose to about 29bp (5y sample), largest rise with NZD and NOK; 3Yx1Y very cheap in the LDI episode and in 2023, then corrected | a stress episode is an outlier regime: winsorise or dummy it before estimating |
| JPY | PC1 response mostly at the long end (0.6bp at 0Yx1Y to 8bp at 15Yx1Y per 1 sd), reflecting YCC and its unwind; 1Yx1Y residual 52.7bp, z 3.82 (text says cheap to US, a figure caption says rich: sources disagree). USDJPY regressions use 2022 dummy interactions (Citi Research, Japan FX: Recent changes in USD/JPY price formation, 15 Jun 2026) | YCC is a break by design: test and split at policy dates; bp vol before and after are different regimes |
| CAD | 1Yx1Y R^2 0.846, residual 145.6bp, z 2.54; the counterexample on PC2 (Fed-following): PC2 beta lower in the 5y sample than in the 10y | betas do not move in the same direction across markets: estimate per market |
| AUD | 1Yx1Y R^2 0.862, residual 193.8bp, z 3.15 | |
| NZD | 1Yx1Y R^2 0.886, residual 174.5bp, z 2.73; PC2 beta from about -50 (long run) to about +55 (last 10y) | sign flip across windows: re-estimate rolling |
| CHF | no time-series evidence in the sources beyond a 10y relative-value z of -1.5 (actual 0.43 vs model 0.71, BofA Apr 2025) | negative-rate era: no logs; treat as a short-sample market |
| SEK, NOK | SEK own-economy HDS beta negative this cycle, 1Yx1Y about -115bp rich to US; NOK 1Yx1Y z 2.46, PC2 beta rose | small markets: short effective samples, wide error bars |
Cross-market rule: rate spreads are governed mostly by the constituent markets' betas to global factors, so instability in either leg's beta is instability of the spread. For seasonality of JGB-linked inflation (CPI ex fresh food seasonal swing "well in excess" of trend) see During, Fixed Income Trading and Risk Management (2021).
Reader inference (not in sources): in zero or negative rate regimes (EUR, CHF, JPY, SEK 2015-22) bp vol and the ACF structure of changes are regime-specific; fit separate GARCH or EWMA parameters per regime or allow a regime-dependent level in the vol equation.
